explanation.title: Spanish Subjunctive Mood: When Doubt, Desire & Emotion Enter

sections.subtitle: Formation of Present Subjunctive
sections.content:
📋 The Opposite Vowel Rule

✅ Formation Steps:
1️⃣ Start with 'yo' form present indicative
2️⃣ Drop -o
3️⃣ Add opposite endings

💡 -AR Verbs (use 'e' endings):
• Endings: -e, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en
→ hablo → hable, hables, hable, hablemos, habléis, hablen

💡 -ER/-IR Verbs (use 'a' endings):
• Endings: -a, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an
→ como → coma, comas, coma, comamos, comáis, coman
→ vivo → viva, vivas, viva, vivamos, viváis, vivan

⚠️ Stem-Changing -IR Verbs:
• Keep changes: e→ie, o→ue
• EXCEPT nosotros/vosotros
→ dormir: duerma, duermas, duerma, durmamos, durmáis, duerman
  (note 'u' in nosotros/vosotros)

sections.subtitle: Irregular Present Subjunctive
sections.content:
📋 Major Irregular Forms

⚠️ Completely Irregular:
• ser: sea, seas, sea, seamos, seáis, sean
• estar: esté, estés, esté, estemos, estéis, estén
• ir: vaya, vayas, vaya, vayamos, vayáis, vayan
• haber: haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayáis, hayan
• saber: sepa, sepas, sepa, sepamos, sepáis, sepan
• dar: dé, des, dé, demos, deis, den

✅ Follow Irregular 'Yo' Pattern:
• tener → tengo → tenga
• venir → vengo → venga
• decir → digo → diga
• hacer → hago → haga
• poner → pongo → ponga
• traer → traigo → traiga
• salir → salgo → salga
• ver → veo → vea
• conocer → conozco → conozca
• conducir → conduzco → conduzca

💡 Pattern: If 'yo' is irregular, subjunctive follows that stem

sections.subtitle: When to Use Subjunctive: WEIRDO Part 1
sections.content:
📋 WEIRDO Triggers - Part 1

💡 W = Wishes/Desires:
• querer que, esperar que, desear que
→ Quiero que vengas (I want you to come)

😊 E = Emotions:
• alegrarse de que, temer que, sentir que, es triste que
→ Me alegro de que estés aquí (I'm glad you're here)

📍 I = Impersonal Expressions:
• es necesario que
• es importante que
• es posible que
• es mejor que
• es bueno/malo que
→ Es importante que estudies (It's important that you study)

⚡ Critical Rule:
Subjunctive appears in the 'que' clause, NOT the main clause!

Pattern: Main clause + QUE + subjunctive clause

sections.subtitle: When to Use Subjunctive: WEIRDO Part 2 & Clauses
sections.content:
📋 WEIRDO Triggers - Part 2

🙏 R = Requests/Recommendations:
• pedir que, sugerir que, recomendar que, aconsejar que
→ Te recomiendo que vayas (I recommend you go)

❓ D = Doubt/Denial:
• dudar que, no creer que, no pensar que, negar que
→ Dudo que venga (I doubt he'll come)

🤞 O = Ojalá (I hope/wish):
→ Ojalá que llueva (I hope it rains)

📋 Special Clauses:

1️⃣ ADJECTIVE CLAUSES (unknown/nonexistent):
→ Busco un libro que sea interesante
  (looking for a book that IS interesting - don't know if exists)

2️⃣ ADVERBIAL CLAUSES:
• para que (so that)
• antes de que (before)
• cuando (when - future)
• aunque (although - hypothetical)

sections.subtitle: Imperfect Subjunctive
sections.content:
📋 Imperfect Subjunctive Formation

✅ Formation Steps:
1️⃣ Start with 3rd person plural preterite (ellos/ellas)
2️⃣ Drop -ron
3️⃣ Add endings: -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -rais, -ran
   OR: -se, -ses, -se, -semos, -seis, -sen

💡 Examples:
→ hablar: hablaron → hablara/hablase
→ comer: comieron → comiera/comiese
→ ser/ir: fueron → fuera/fuese
→ tener: tuvieron → tuviera/tuviese

🎯 Three Main Uses:

1️⃣ Hypothetical 'if' clauses:
→ Si tuviera dinero, compraría un coche
  (If I had money, I would buy a car)

2️⃣ Past subjunctive triggers:
→ Quería que vinieras
  (I wanted you to come)

3️⃣ Sequence of tenses:
→ When main verb is past, use imperfect subjunctive in dependent clause

sections.subtitle: Perfect Subjunctive
sections.content:
📋 Perfect Subjunctive Forms

✅ PRESENT PERFECT SUBJUNCTIVE:
• haber (present subjunctive) + past participle
• Forms: haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayáis, hayan

💡 Uses:
→ Past actions in subjunctive contexts connected to present
→ Espero que hayas estudiado (I hope you have studied)
→ Dudo que haya llegado (I doubt he has arrived)

⚠️ PLUPERFECT SUBJUNCTIVE:
• haber (imperfect subjunctive) + past participle
• Forms: hubiera/hubiese + past participle

💡 Uses:
→ Past perfect in subjunctive contexts
→ Si hubiera sabido, habría venido
  (If I had known, I would have come)

🎯 Common Pattern:
Pluperfect subjunctive often pairs with conditional perfect in past hypotheticals

Pattern: Si + pluperfect subjunctive, conditional perfect

questions.question: How do you form the present subjunctive for -AR verbs?
questions.hint: -AR verbs use the 'opposite' vowel (e instead of a) in subjunctive.

questions.question: How do you form the present subjunctive for -ER/-IR verbs?
questions.hint: -ER/-IR verbs use the 'opposite' vowel (a instead of e/i) in subjunctive.

questions.question: What is the present subjunctive 'yo' form of 'hablar'?
questions.hint: Start with hablo, drop -o, add -e. Result: hable.

questions.question: What is the present subjunctive 'yo' form of 'comer'?
questions.hint: Start with como, drop -o, add -a. Result: coma.

questions.question: What is the irregular present subjunctive 'yo' form of 'ser'?
questions.hint: Ser is completely irregular. All forms use 'sea' as the stem.

questions.question: What is the irregular present subjunctive 'yo' form of 'ir'?
questions.hint: Ir is completely irregular. All forms use 'vay' as the stem + endings.

questions.question: What is the present subjunctive 'yo' form of 'tener' (has irregular yo: tengo)?
questions.hint: Start with irregular yo form 'tengo', drop -o, add -a: tenga.

questions.question: 'Quiero que vengas' - Why use subjunctive?
questions.hint: 'Quiero que' (I want that) expresses a wish/desire, triggering subjunctive.

questions.question: 'Me alegro de que estés aquí' - Why use subjunctive?
questions.hint: 'Me alegro de que' (I'm glad that) expresses emotion, triggering subjunctive.

questions.question: 'Es importante que estudies' - Why use subjunctive?
questions.hint: 'Es importante que' is an impersonal expression, triggering subjunctive.

questions.question: 'Dudo que venga' - Why use subjunctive?
questions.hint: 'Dudo que' (I doubt that) expresses doubt/uncertainty, triggering subjunctive.

questions.question: 'Te recomiendo que vayas' - Why use subjunctive?
questions.hint: 'Recomiendo que' (I recommend that) is a recommendation, triggering subjunctive.

questions.question: 'Busco un libro que sea interesante' - Why use subjunctive?

answers.text: Talking about a specific known book

questions.hint: Don't know if such a book exists. Unknown antecedent triggers subjunctive.

questions.question: 'Estudio para que aprendas' means 'I study so that you learn' - Why subjunctive after 'para que'?
questions.hint: 'Para que' (so that) introduces purpose/goal, triggering subjunctive.

questions.question: How do you form the imperfect subjunctive?

answers.text: 3rd person plural preterite minus -ron, add -ra endings

questions.hint: Start with the 'ellos' preterite form: hablaron→hablara, comieron→comiera.

questions.question: What is the imperfect subjunctive 'yo' form of 'hablar' (preterite: hablaron)?
questions.hint: hablaron → habla- → hablara. Two forms exist: -ra or -se endings.

questions.question: What is the imperfect subjunctive 'yo' form of 'ser/ir' (preterite: fueron)?
questions.hint: fueron → fue- → fuera. Ser and ir share same imperfect subjunctive forms.

questions.question: 'Si tuviera dinero, compraría un coche' - What tenses are used and why?
questions.hint: 'Si' + imperfect subjunctive + conditional = hypothetical present/future.

questions.question: 'Quería que vinieras' - Why use imperfect subjunctive?

answers.text: Main verb is past (quería), so use imperfect subjunctive

questions.hint: Sequence of tenses: past main verb requires imperfect (not present) subjunctive.

questions.question: How do you form the present perfect subjunctive?
questions.hint: Use haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayáis, hayan + past participle.

questions.question: 'Espero que hayas estudiado' means...
questions.hint: Present perfect subjunctive: past action with present relevance. Hayas = you have.

questions.question: How do you form the pluperfect subjunctive?
questions.hint: Use hubiera/hubiese + past participle. Past perfect in subjunctive contexts.

questions.question: 'Si hubiera sabido, habría venido' means...

answers.text: If I had known, I would have come
If I know, I will come
If I knew, I would come

questions.hint: Pluperfect subjunctive + conditional perfect = past hypothetical/regret.

questions.question: Which requires subjunctive: 'Sé que viene' or 'Dudo que venga'?
questions.hint: Certainty (sé que) uses indicative. Doubt (dudo que) uses subjunctive.
